## Statement

Two balanced Heegaard diagrams of the same marked sutured manifold are connected by relative attaching-circle isotopies, own-family disk slides, and ordinary stabilizations and destabilizations. An ordinary stabilization can be moved by such slides to the true boundary region. These moves induce integral chain homotopy equivalences for the transported coherent orientation class. The product sutured manifold has integral homology equal to one copy of the integers; on a homology-product branch the periodic-domain character ambiguity vanishes.

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, and suppose $Y\setminus K$ fibers over $S^1$ with connected fiber a Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Then the integral top Alexander group is one copy of the integers:

$$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z.$$
[F3] [[lem-relative-sutured-diagrams-have-signed-move-equivalences]] gives the signed comparison for the specified transported orientation class and computes the product by the empty diagram.

1.1 Use the actual binding bridge and drilling construction to represent the exterior with two meridional sutures, carrying the actual page longitude and the class of F. The adapted surface cut is literally the result of cutting this mapping torus along its fiber, hence is F times an interval with its product sutures. Apply the finite permissible niceification. Signed relative diagram moves compare the resulting complex to the chosen defining complex, with its specified coherent orientation class transported. No restriction on Y or change of coefficient ring is made. [F1, F2, F3]

3.1 The empty diagram of the actual product has one empty-tuple generator and no nonconstant disk, so its integral chain complex is Z with zero differential. The signed relative move equivalences identify its homology with that of the actual cut diagram. Combining with the full top-summand chain identification gives the asserted integral group isomorphism. The exterior orientation character restricts trivially to the zero-periodic cut, so this conclusion holds for the specified defining class without asserting equivalence of arbitrary orientation systems on the uncut exterior. [F3, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $g(K)$ be the least genus of a compact connected oriented embedded surface in $S^3$ with boundary $K$. With the integral Alexander normalization, the maximum Alexander grading in which the hat knot Floer homology of $K$ is nonzero is $g(K)$:

$$g(K)=\max\{i\in\mathbb Z:\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^3,K,i;\mathbb Z)\ne0\}.$$

[F6] **Classical analytic input and exact axiom boundary.** Under the Axiom of Choice in the Statement, use the general integral sutured analytic framework explicitly imported in F5 of [[lem-integral-sutured-floer-compactness-and-orientations]], at the actual balanced/adapted diagrams, admissibility, boundary-region/divisor and coherent-orientation conditions of F2–F4. This supplies the pointwise Fredholm, regularity, compactification and strip/polygon gluing prerequisite; the preserved local area, grading, signed cut and hierarchy constructions then use it at their stated targets. The published framework is Juhász, *Holomorphic discs and sutured manifolds*, §§3,6–7, especially Definition7.1 and Theorems7.2/7.5, together with the referenced Ozsváth–Szabó analytic framework, and Juhász, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, Proposition7.6 and Theorems1.4–1.5. These are explicit external inputs in the classical setting, not a newly reconstructed weak-choice theorem. [[lem-countable-analytic-choice-for-fixed-sutured-floer-data]] retains its conditional Countable Choice conclusion: GIVEN the actual pointwise constructions, its fixed finite diagram/cut and at-most-two-parameter choices are finite or countable. It does not itself prove that those pointwise constructions follow under Countable Choice. The Countable-Choice-only genus strengthening is not certified here; neither its falsity nor an independent new geometric open problem is asserted. [Juhász2006](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf), [Juhász2008](https://msp.org/gt/2008/12-1/gt-v12-n1-p07-s.pdf)

3.1 Work under the full-Choice analytic framework F6 on the actual fixed finite hierarchy and marked adapted diagram. Its admitted sutured operator problems retain the boundary/divisor barriers, periodic-domain and area conditions and the specified coherent orientation class. With the regular data and compactification/gluing construction supplied at that scope, apply F3 to the marked Seifert surface F. Its meridional frame, rather than an unspecified closure framing, gives an admissible adapted representative. By F4 every generator has Alexander degree g−n_P(x), with n_P(x) a nonnegative integer. Hence its whole integral chain complex has no generator, and thus no homology, in a grading greater than g. [F3, F4, F6, step 2.1]
